sentences.text: Burundi -LRB- -LSB- bəˈrʊndi -RSB- or -LSB- bəˈrʌndi -RSB- -RRB- , officially the Republic of Burundi -LRB- Republika y' Uburundi , -LSB- buˈɾundi -RSB- République du Burundi , -LSB- buʁundi -RSB- or -LSB- byʁyndi -RSB- -RRB- , is a landlocked country in the African Great Lakes region of East Africa , bordered by Rwanda to the north , Tanzania to the east and south , and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west .	landlocked country	landlocked country	African Great Lakes	African Great Lakes	East Africa	East Africa	Rwanda	Rwanda	Tanzania	Tanzania	Democratic Republic of the Congo	Democratic Republic of the Congo
It is also considered part of Central Africa .	Central Africa	Central Africa
Burundi 's capital is Bujumbura .	Bujumbura	Bujumbura
The southwestern border is adjacent to Lake Tanganyika .	Lake Tanganyika	Lake Tanganyika
The Twa , Hutu and Tutsi peoples have lived in Burundi for at least 500 years .	Hutu	Hutu	Tutsi	Tutsi	Twa	Twa
For more than 200 of those years , Burundi was an independent kingdom , until the beginning of the 20th century , when Germany colonised the region .	kingdom	Kingdom of Burundi	Germany	German Empire
After the First World War and Germany 's defeat , it ceded the territory to Belgium .	Belgium	Belgium	Germany	German Empire	First World War	First World War
Both Germans and Belgians ruled Burundi and Rwanda as a European colony known as Ruanda-Urundi .	Ruanda-Urundi	Ruanda-Urundi	Rwanda	Rwanda
Despite common misconceptions , Burundi and Rwanda had never been under common rule until the time of European colonisation .	Rwanda	Rwanda

Burundi gained independence in 1962 and initially had a monarchy , but a series of assassinations , coups and a general climate of regional instability culminated in the establishment of a republic and one-party state in 1966 .	republic	republic	monarchy	Kingdom of Burundi	regional instability	Congo Crisis

Bouts of ethnic cleansing and ultimately two civil wars and genocides during the 1970s and again in the 1990s left the country undeveloped and its population as one of the world 's poorest .	ethnic cleansing	ethnic cleansing	1970s	Burundian Genocide#1972	1990s	Burundian Civil War

2015 witnessed large-scale political strife as President Pierre Nkurunziza opted to run for a third term in office , a coup attempt failed and the country 's parliamentary and presidential elections were broadly criticised by members of the international community .	President	List of Presidents of Burundi	Pierre Nkurunziza	Pierre Nkurunziza	large-scale political strife	2015 Burundian unrest	coup attempt failed	2015 Burundian coup d'état attempt	parliamentary	Burundian legislative election, 2015	presidential	Presidential system

Burundi 's political system is that of a presidential representative democratic republic based upon a multi-party state .	republic	republic	presidential	Presidential system	representative democratic	Representative democracy
The President of Burundi is the head of state and head of government .	President	List of Presidents of Burundi	head of state	head of state	head of government	head of government
There are currently 21 registered parties in Burundi .	registered parties in Burundi	List of political parties in Burundi

On 13 March 1992 , Tutsi coup leader Pierre Buyoya established a constitution , which provided for a multi-party political process and reflected multi-party competition .	Tutsi	Tutsi	Pierre Buyoya	Pierre Buyoya
Six years later , on 6 June 1998 , the constitution was changed , broadening National Assembly 's seats and making provisions for two vice-presidents .	National Assembly	National Assembly of Burundi
Because of the Arusha Accord , Burundi enacted a transitional government in 2000 .	Arusha Accord	Arusha Accord
In October 2016 , Burundi informed the UN of its intention to withdraw from the International Criminal Court .	International Criminal Court	International Criminal Court
Burundi remains an overwhelmingly rural society , with just 13 % of the population living in urban areas in 2013 .
The population density of around 315 people per square kilometre -LRB- 753 per sq mi -RRB- is the second highest in Sub-Saharan Africa .	Sub-Saharan Africa	Sub-Saharan Africa
Roughly 85 % of the population are of Hutu ethnic origin , 15 % are Tutsi , and fewer than 1 % are indigenous Twa -LRB- or Pygmies -RRB- .	Hutu	Hutu	Tutsi	Tutsi	Twa	Twa
The official languages of Burundi are French and Kirundi , although Swahili can be found spoken along the Tanzanian border .	French	French language	Kirundi	Kirundi language
One of the smallest countries in Africa , Burundi has an equatorial climate .	equatorial climate	equatorial climate
Burundi is a part of the Albertine Rift , the western extension of the East African Rift .	Albertine Rift	Albertine Rift	East African Rift	East African Rift
The country lies on a rolling plateau in the centre of Africa .	plateau	plateau
The highest peak , Mount Heha at 8810 ft , lies to the southeast of the capital , Bujumbura .	Bujumbura	Bujumbura	Mount Heha	Mount Heha

The source of the River Nile is in Bururi province , and is linked from Lake Victoria to its headwaters via the Ruvyironza River Another major lake is Lake Tanganyika , located in much of Burundi 's southwestern corner .	Lake Tanganyika	Lake Tanganyika	River Nile	River Nile	Lake Victoria	Lake Victoria	Ruvyironza River	Ruvyironza River

There are two national parks , Kibira National Park to the northwest -LRB- a small region of rain forest , adjacent to Nyungwe Forest National Park in Rwanda -RRB- , Ruvubu National Park to the northeast -LRB- along the Rurubu River , also known as Ruvubu or Ruvuvu -RRB- .	Rwanda	Rwanda	Kibira National Park	Kibira National Park	Nyungwe Forest National Park	Nyungwe Forest National Park	Ruvubu National Park	Ruvubu National Park	Rurubu River	Rurubu River
Both were established in 1982 to conserve wildlife populations .	wildlife	wildlife
Burundi 's lands are mostly agricultural or pasture .
Settlement by rural populations has led to deforestation , soil erosion and habitat loss .	deforestation	deforestation	soil erosion	soil erosion	habitat loss	habitat loss
Deforestation of the entire country is almost completely due to overpopulation , with a mere 230 mi2 remaining and an ongoing loss of about 9 % per annum .	overpopulation	Human overpopulation
In addition to poverty , Burundians often have to deal with corruption , weak infrastructure , poor access to health and education services , and hunger .
Burundi is densely populated and has had substantial emigration as young people seek opportunities elsewhere .	emigration	emigration
The World Happiness Report 2017 ranked Burundi as the world 's second least happy nation with a rank of 154 .	World Happiness Report 2017	World Happiness Report	nation	nation
